video_title: Is A Market Breakdown Underway? | Katie Stockton
gist: Technician Katie Stockton (Fairlead Strategies) says last week's AI-led selloff has broken Nasdaq 100 support but not yet the S&P 500's, and a breakdown would be confirmed only if the index fails to rebound from oversold levels this week. Support sits about 7% lower (near the 200-day and ~7,240 Fibonacci level). Credit spreads are uncomfortably close to a breakout that would make H1 2027 difficult. Her long-term trend stays bullish. Gold is downtrending but DeMark signals a near-term low near $3,900, and a WTI breakout above $105 would be another equity risk.

insights.claim: Host Adam Taggart notes that four of the Mag 7 stocks are in bear-market territory, the Mag 7 has lost about $4 trillion in market cap, and well over 60% of S&P 500 stocks are more than 20% below their all-time highs, even though the S&P is still up for the year.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Market breadth is much weaker than the headline index suggests.

insights.claim: Stockton says the Nasdaq 100 has fallen below the support level Fairlead was watching, while the S&P 500, Fairlead's primary input, still has some room, so the breakdown is not yet decisive.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: The S&P 500 is near support but not yet broken.
insights.quote: we wouldn't call this a decisive breakdown yet

insights.claim: Stockton's confirmation rule: if the Nasdaq 100 fails this week to deliver the rebound that oversold readings suggest, she will take that as the market confirming the breakdowns.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: She gives a clear near-term trigger for turning more defensive.
insights.quote: If we don't see that rebound that the oversold metrics would suggest, uh then I think that's probably a message from the market that we have breakdowns being confirmed

insights.claim: Stockton says that if breakdowns are confirmed, the next support levels sit on average about 7% below current levels. For the S&P 500 that means the 200-day moving average and a Fibonacci retracement near 7,240.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: This gives a rough measure of downside risk if the breakdown is confirmed.
insights.quote: I would say I'd put them in on average maybe 7% below the current levels

insights.claim: Stockton says short-term stochastics are oversold, which supports near-term stabilization, but weekly (intermediate-term) oversold conditions are not yet widespread, so the decline could still deepen.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: A short-term bounce would not mean the correction is over.

insights.claim: DeMark buy signals on the major indices have not triggered because they require a deeper, more prolonged decline. Among individual stocks, MGM generated one after 17 consecutive down weeks.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: No technical bottom signal has appeared in the indices yet.

insights.claim: Going into the midterm elections, Stockton views the oversold, fearful tape as favorable: a market that hasn't run up beforehand finds a positive reaction easier, and any relief of uncertainty tends to be welcomed.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: The market setup favors a relief rally after the election.

insights.claim: Stockton says the long-term (cyclical/secular) uptrend remains intact on slow indicators such as the monthly MACD, and that being a secular bull is almost always right. Any break now would most likely be a healthy reset within the uptrend.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: A correction is a time to hedge, not to sell out.

insights.claim: Credit spreads are Stockton's biggest macro-technical input. They are elevated and testing historical resistance, and a breakout has historically marked very significant corrections or bear markets even without recession.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: Credit spreads are the key gauge for a larger equity drawdown.

insights.claim: Stockton predicts that if credit spreads break out, which she says they are uncomfortably close to doing, the first half of 2027 will probably be difficult for equities.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: Investors should watch credit spreads closely going into 2027.
insights.quote: if credit spreads break out, and they're pretty close, uncomfortably close, I would say, well, that probably means the first half of 2027 will be difficult

insights.claim: Fairlead's own systematic ETF has shifted to a bigger risk-off stance than at any point this year, partly moving into Treasuries after being mostly in equities.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: Fairlead's systematic models are cutting risk.

insights.claim: Despite the risks, Stockton would not rule out a stronger year-end finish: Q4 and especially November seasonality is strong, breadth is improving, retailers are breaking above resistance as tech tests support, and small caps are recovering.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: Rotation under the surface could support a year-end rally.
insights.quote: I wouldn't rule out a stronger finish to the year

insights.claim: Stockton calls this a mature, concentrated, tech-led bull market after four straight years of double-digit gains, which suggests more muted returns ahead, but she would not make a call on cycles alone.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: Investors should expect lower future returns rather than a crash.

insights.claim: The Fear and Greed Index is around 25, in extreme-fear territory, which Stockton reads as a contrarian positive partly offset by weak breadth.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: Sentiment is far from bullish, which supports the case for a bounce.

insights.claim: Taggart argues AI stock prices can deflate while AI capex keeps rising, citing Jan van Eck (compute demand still far outstrips supply) and FreightWaves CEO Craig Fuller (no slowdown in shipments of data-center materials).
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: A selloff in AI stocks may not mean AI investment spending is slowing.

insights.claim: Stockton agrees markets can diverge from the economy for long periods, but notes bear markets have historically been linked to weaker economies, sometimes with significant leads or lags.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: She would follow the price trend rather than economic narratives.

insights.claim: Taggart says AI and AI-related stocks are approaching about 50% of the S&P 500's market cap, so their weakness has outweighed strong recent performance in value stocks.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Index investors carry concentrated AI exposure.

insights.claim: Stockton says there has been a secular shift higher in yields, confirmed by long-term trend thresholds and a recently completed triangle in Treasury yields. She expects yields and bond prices to move sideways in the near term, which preserves capital for fixed income.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: Bonds now work as portfolio ballast again.
insights.quote: we think there's been a secular shift higher in yields

insights.claim: Fairlead's ETF holds both 1–3 year and long-term Treasuries. Stockton prefers the short end on relative strength, though she says this is a technical rather than macro view.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: Shorter-maturity Treasuries are favored for now.

insights.claim: Gold is in a downtrend after its blow-off top earlier this year, but DeMark indicators and other oversold measures suggest a near-term low is within reach. Stockton puts support around $3,900 an ounce, with further support near $3,600.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: A small gold position is reasonable for diversification, but not as a trend trade.
insights.quote: That could help preserve the support, which for us is around 3,900 per ounce

insights.claim: To turn positive on gold, Stockton would want stabilization and evidence that buyers are stepping in, such as a reclaim of the 20- or 50-day moving average, rather than buying into the decline.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: She would wait for confirmation rather than catch a falling knife.

insights.claim: Stockton says WTI crude, topical because of the Iran war, has formed a large triangle after a long-term upward momentum shift. A breakout above $105 a barrel would be another risk signal for equities.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: $105 WTI is a key level that would signal more risk for equities.
insights.quote: if we were to see a breakout from the triangle, which would happen above $105 per barrel

insights.claim: Taggart reports headline speculation that the US administration may escalate the Iran conflict again after the midterms, which could push oil prices higher.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Geopolitical risk to oil prices may rise after the election.

insights.claim: Stockton recommends diversification toward lower-beta, lower-correlation and defensive exposure while still holding tech stocks as long as they keep their support levels, with small positions in fixed income, gold and Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: Her stance is a balanced risk-reduction tilt, not a full exit from stocks.

insights.claim: Fairlead's latest ideas favor the retail sector, which has strong November seasonality and improving momentum, interest-rate-sensitive homebuilders on a short horizon, and turnarounds in the defense sector.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: Former laggards could lead into year-end.

insights.claim: Stockton stays underweight international equities relative to the US but looks for country-level breakouts, citing a gap in Brazil that looked vulnerable to being filled.
insights.speaker: Katie Stockton
insights.so_what: No broad case for international stocks yet, only individual country trades.
